dict.string: Sends pasted text to a taskpaper file
Add a task to todo.taskpaper inbox

#A really simple Taskpaper workflow
1. Set your .taskpaper todo file location here 2. Set a project header for your task inbox 3. Summon with keyword (default is tdx) 4. Type your todo 5. Hit return, and it will be added to the top your inbox project in your TaskPaper file
Set target .taskpaper file and inbox project: in this Workflow configuration.
Need more space to type? Action the keyword with option-enter (⌥-⏎) to bring up a text entry box.
## Input handling:
- Lines already formatted (start with tab + dash): inserted as-is - Raw text lines: wrapped as a bare task with @date - Blank lines: skipped - If heading not found: prepended tasks to top of file
### File path:
- default is ~/todo.taskpaper (in Alfred) - set in Alfred with {var:targetfile} - hardcoded default is ~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~hogbaysoftware~TaskPaper/Documents/todo.taskpaper - pass --file to override.
### Inbox project heading:
- defaults to _INBOX: - set in Alfred by {var:inbox}
## Technical details
Alfred Variables are:
{var:targetfile} {var:inbox}
Usage (terminal):
python3 /path/to/inbox.py "Buy more charcoal" echo "some text" | python3 inbox.py
Usage (Alfred — zsh, pipe via stdin for an external script):
query=$1 echo "$1" | python3 /path/to/inbox.py
Set the Keyword for this Workflow

Select your .taskpaper file to add tasks. It will default to todo.taskpaper in either your ~/ home directory, or the top level of your iCloud drive TaskPaper folder if the script is used from the command line.
Set the project within your .taskpaper file. Tasks are added at the top of this project. It should end with a colon : Default is _INBOX:
